messages.content: Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.
Explain in exactly three sentences why floating-point addition is not associative.

samples.text: Floating-point numbers have limited precision, so each operation rounds the exact real result to the nearest representable value. Because the rounding error depends on the magnitude of the operands, adding a small number to a large one may be lost, while adding the small number after an intermediate sum can change the final rounding. Consequently, (a + b) + c and a + (b + c) can produce different floating‑point results, breaking associativity.
